text:
customer-acme: Hey team — we've got a production issue. Over the last hour our embeddings client started failing intermittently with \"dimension mismatch\" when consuming batched responses. We send a batch of 12 texts, and ~2/12 responses come back as 1024-dim vectors while the rest are 1536. Our downstream code assumes 1536 and crashes. No config changed on our side. Any quick ideas?

sara: Thanks — sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK) and a sample request id from a failed batch? Also which model name are you calling?

customer-acme: We're calling `embed-verified-1536` via the hosted endpoint. Example curl (redacted keys):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\  -d '{"model":"embed-verified-1536","input":["short text A","short text B", "long text that will be tokenized to a lot more tokens...", "... (total 12 items)"], "batching": {"dynamic": true}}'
```

Failed request id header from our logs: `req_20260315_acme_9172`

sara: Got it — thanks. @pranay / @oliver can you check routing logs for `req_20260315_acme_9172`? Suspect routing might have mixed a fallback variant into the same coalesced batch.

pranay: Looking. I can see the batch coalescer grouped 12 client items into a single kernel batch. In the trace it shows model assignment: 10 shards -> `embed-verified-1536`, 2 shards -> `embed-lite-1024` (fallback). That means different requests in same coalesced batch executed on different backends but responses were assembled into one response array — client-side then sees mixed dims.

oliver: Quick context: dynamic routing can fallback to a lower-dimension variant under resource pressure (qps spike + GPU mem) if policy allows. Our batcher had an affinity bug where per-request model affinity wasn't enforced before coalescing, so mixed-variant shards ended up in the same batch id. That's the likely root cause.

customer-acme: Is that why only some entries are 1024? Makes sense. Can you confirm why fallback happened? We didn't ask for fallback explicitly.

pranay: The fallback happened because two requests had very large tokenized lengths (the long text) causing placement to choose `embed-lite-1024` to fit memory/latency targets. The batcher then naively coalesced by time-window and max_batch_size without checking uniform model_variant.

lena: Also seeing tail latency spike in metrics at the same time — the single huge padded sequence increased runtime and pushed capacity, leading to fallbacks. So it's twofold: (1) mixed-variant coalescing bug, (2) oversized sequences causing tail latency and fallback pressure.

sara: Action plan for immediate mitigation: 1) Tell customer to temporarily set `batching.dynamic=false` or set `max_batch_size=6` on their request to avoid large coalesced groups. 2) We'll add a short-term server-side guard to reject mixing variants in the same coalesced batch. 3) Engineering will deploy a fix to the affinity check.

customer-acme: We can toggle `dynamic=false` now — will that preserve throughput? We care about latency as well.

pranay: Setting `dynamic=false` will send batches immediate per-requesty batching (client-side size) — likely lower throughput but much more predictable dims. Alternatively, set `max_batch_size` to 4–6 and enable `pad_to_multiple=64` to reduce expensive padding effects.

oliver: For reproducibility, here's a short repro we used to reproduce locally (approx):

```python
# pseudo repro: create a wide length variance payload
inputs = ["short text"] * 10 + ["long * 2000 tokens content"] * 2
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-verified-1536", input=inputs, batching={"dynamic": True, "max_batch_size": 12})
# inspect shapes
for i, v in enumerate(resp.data):
    print(i, len(v.embedding))  # expect all 1536 but see 1024 for some
```

lena: I opened INC-2026 and linked the trace. Also firing an alert rule: `embeddings.mixed_variant_errors > 0` and `embeddings.tail_latency_p95 > 2s` (temporary).

oliver: Hotfix plan: 1) add variant affinity check in coalescer (reject/hold if different target variants), 2) enforce padding caps and prefer splitting oversized sequences across batches, 3) validate assembled batch embeddings dims and return 500 with clear error if mismatch (safer than sending mixed dims). Can do quick rollout to canary within 2 hours.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of coalescer affinity patch started by oliver at 2026-03-15T18:45:00Z (canary: 10% traffic).

customer-acme: Appreciate the fast response. We'll set `batching.dynamic=false` for the next 24h and increase client-side retries. Please keep us posted on the canary.

sara: Will do. @oliver update us when canary hits prod. Also can customer share a failing request id: `req_20260315_acme_9172` was helpful — we attached the trace to the ticket.

oliver: Canary looks good — no mixed-dim responses in 10k test requests. Rolling to 50% next.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026 updated: mitigation in progress, status = investigating -> mitigating.

lena: Postmortem notes (quick): root cause is coalescer not enforcing model_variant affinity; secondary factor was extreme token-length variance causing fallback variant assignment. Long-term: improve routing policy to prefer model homogeneity per coalesced batch and add client docs recommending max per-request token length or per-request max_batch_size hints.

customer-acme: Thanks — will follow the doc suggestions. Let us know when full rollout is done and we'll revert our temporary client change.

oliver: Full rollout completed at 2026-03-15T19:22:00Z. Closing the incident when we get zero mixed-dim hits for 1 hour.

sara: Closing loop: customer happy. Ticket notes: customer set dynamic batching off temporarily; we deployed coalescer fix and added an alert.

customer-acme: Confirmed no more failures since ~19:30 UTC — thanks everyone :tada:
